Who this trip suits

An offshore charter suits a group that accepts open-water motion, travel time and a target that can change with conditions. Choose the boat around the least comfortable person in the party. Ask about shade, a toilet, seating and a way to rest.

For a first sea trip, compare an inshore or nearshore option before you commit to a long offshore day. Tell the crew about limited mobility and any concern about motion. Ask a pharmacist or clinician about motion-sickness options if you need advice.

Choose offshore, reef or wreck fishing

Scroll the table to compare all columns.

TripDecision that mattersQuestion for the crew
Offshore pelagic tripTrolling, live bait, casting or jigging can produce very different participation.Who handles the rods, and how do anglers take turns?
Reef or bottom tripDepth, tackle and the target differ from open-water trolling.What depth and physical effort should our party expect?
Wreck tripThe word describes structure, not a complete target or method.Which species, technique and legal area does this proposal cover?

When to go

FWC’s Monroe County overview points to spring–summer for dolphinfish, also called mahi-mahi. It lists fall–spring for sailfish and blackfin tuna. Treat these as broad trip-selection clues.

Pick the target first, then ask the crew what is realistic in the proposed week. Do not convert a seasonal occurrence into a promise of retention. Review the Keys marine forecast, including winds, waves and warnings. A sunny land forecast does not describe the offshore route.

Source: FWC: where to saltwater fish — Monroe County · NWS: Florida Keys marine forecasts · NWS: understand a marine forecast

How to compare the actual outing

Name the departure island and marina. Confirm whether the quoted time runs from dock departure to return, and ask for the likely travel portion. No fixed run time applies across all Keys boats and grounds.

Compare a shared boat and a private charter by space, participation and the agreed target. Ask what happens if the captain cancels, returns early or proposes an inshore substitute. Record whether a substitute needs your agreement and how the charge changes. Leave a margin before a flight or other fixed appointment.

What the crew provides: get the detail

Request the tackle list for the chosen method: rods, reels, terminal tackle, bait and any fighting support. Confirm crew help with rigging and fish handling. A guest should not buy heavy offshore tackle before the captain approves it.

Ask about drinking water, ice, food, fish cleaning, storage and any additional charge. These are quote questions, not standard inclusions. For a U.S. passenger charter, request the captain’s credential and safety plan, plus the vessel inspection document where applicable.

Source: US Coast Guard: checks before a passenger charter

Local mistakes to avoid

  • Comparing a short reef trip with a long offshore trip by price alone.
  • Assuming a “wreck charter” means a specific species or a hands-on casting day.
  • Treating the whole Florida Keys chain as one departure point.
  • Using a land weather app to approve an offshore outing.
  • Planning to keep a target fish before checking the current area and species rules.

Regulations and licenses

Check Florida visitor rules and the boat’s saltwater charter license coverage. Use the current FWC species pages and NOAA sanctuary guidance for the planned fishing area.

For Atlantic highly migratory species, including relevant tuna and billfish trips, ask the captain about the applicable NOAA permits and current notices. The captain must confirm the vessel’s permissions; this page does not verify an operator.

Source: FWC: visitor licenses · FWC: saltwater charter license coverage · FWC: saltwater recreational regulations · NOAA: Florida Keys sanctuary fishing regulations · NOAA Fisheries: Atlantic highly migratory species, for-hire fishing

Questions and answers

Is a reef charter the same as an offshore charter?

No. Ask for the actual target, depth, method and travel time. A reef or wreck label alone does not describe the day.

What season suits mahi-mahi in the Keys?

FWC’s Monroe County overview identifies spring–summer as a broad reference. Weather, target availability and current rules still control the actual trip.

Should I bring my own offshore rod?

Only after the crew confirms the complete setup fits the method and boat. Ask for the supplied tackle inventory first.
